text.p: The dollar, holding on to most of the gains it scored on Tuesday, is now set to attack key resistance at 1.7530 marks and 115.50 yen, analysts said.
"Dollar/mark pulled back to 1.7152 on June 24 before rising again. We have not looked back since," stressed MCM CurrencyWatch senior analyst Scott Siller.
"The New York action is positive," added Siller who pointed out dollar/mark and dollar/yen gave up little ground in New York after setting recent highs in Asia and Europe.
At 2000 GMT, the dollar traded at 1.7465/70 marks versus 1.7455/60 at the open, and at 114.87/92 yen vs. 114.90/00.
Dollar/mark rose to a fresh 40-month high of 1.7488 in Europe, topping Monday's 1.7465 -- itself the highest level since the week ended on February 20, 1994.

Chartists said the dollar/mark's ability to hold above Monday's 1.7465 high was a positive on the way to a strong resistance in the 1.7520/30 area. The 1.7520 level is the upper end of a rising channel from April and 1.7530 is the next 1994 high, also recorded in the February 20 week.
Next is the 1994 peak set on February 8, at 1.7686.
"I don't see 1.7686 right away, but 1.7520/30 marks is possible," Siller said.
Another bullish development for dollar/mark is the dollar/Swiss rally, often a good indicator of the dollar's future performance versus the European currencies.
"Dollar/Swiss is rising above 1.4660. That's a trendline resistance dating back to the March 6 high of 1.4922. It's another positive for dollar/mark," Siller said.
Dollar/mark is likely to find added strength in a weak mark/yen, struggling above critical support at 65.55 after faltering short of 66.00 resistance, chartists said.
Mark/yen weakness mirrored fresh strength in dollar/yen that rose to 115.29 in Asia, the highest since June 23.
"Mark/yen could not break 66.00. It's in a descending triangle with a 65.55 key support," Siller explained.
"For dollar/yen, the whole pattern is a bullish symmetrical triangle, testing 115.30 on the upper end," added the MCM analyst added who saw a possible push to 115.50.
The next level is 117.00 yen, the recent high on May 28. It also is the 38-percent retracement of the 127.47 to 110.62 move -- the 1997 high set on May 1 to the low on June 11.
The dollar was also strong against sterling as cable violated psychological support at $1.66 while the next technical prop is at $1.6545.
